causes: [PROSPECTIVE] Penal Code §290.46(j)(2)(E) — if TaskUs obtains or uses California sex offender registry information in the hiring decision

claims: PC §290.46(j)(2)(E) (prospective — use of registry info in hiring); ICRAA §§1786.16, 1786.40 (prospective); FCRA §§1681b(b)(3), 1681d (prospective); UCL §17200 (prospective)
damages: Prospective. Offer of Temporary Employment (TaskUs, LLC, signed Sep. 14, 2026) states $22.00 per hour, non-exempt, San Jose delivery; anticipated assignment Sep. 23, 2026 through on or around Dec. 4, 2026; $1,000 retention bonus if still employed in good standing on Dec. 4. Statutory framework if the claim ripens: Penal Code §290.46(j)(4)(A) (actual or treble damages, $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages); ICRAA §§1786.50, 1786.52; FCRA §§1681n, 1681o; UCL restitution. No valuation until adverse action, if any.
defendants: TaskUs, LLC (prospective; offer-letter employer, 1650 Independence Drive, Ste 100, New Braunfels, TX 78132); TaskUs USA LLC (prospective; background-consent recipient); TaskUs Holdings, Inc. Uber AV is the WorkDay campaign (R_2608_10812), not a named prospective defendant on this packet — the 2810.5 does not list Uber as the entity for whom the work is performed. DOES 1–10 for other hiring decision-makers if adverse action follows.

key_facts: On Sep. 14, 2026, TaskUs, LLC sent Brendan Ngwa Nforbi a signed Offer of Temporary Employment as a Teammate at $22.00 per hour (non-exempt), location USA - San Jose - San Jose (Delivery). Anticipated assignment Sep. 23, 2026 through on or around Dec. 4, 2026; $1,000 retention bonus if still employed in good standing on Dec. 4. Orientation Sep. 23–25 at 1631 N 1st Street, Suite 200, San Jose; production depot 3030 Corvin Dr., Santa Clara; closed-course training in Sonoma. The offer is at-will, contingent on job-related background screening and a Fair Chance Act process for conviction history, and says screening usually takes two weeks and employment may begin while screening is pending. The same day he signed the United States Background Consent Form (release of screening information to TaskUs USA LLC), the TaskUs Holdings, Inc. NDA/invention-assignment, and a Mutual Arbitration Agreement with TaskUs, Inc. whose covered claims include the background-check form or process. Page 9 of the offer is a California medical-release for drug/alcohol testing facilitated by First Advantage. That is not a consumer-report authorization. No ICRAA/FCRA standalone disclosure is in this packet, no registry or criminal consumer report has been furnished, and no adverse action has occurred. WorkDay requisition R_2608_10812 is 'Uber AV Teammate (SJ: 09/23/2026)' (candidate C261051599). Uber AV is the client campaign. It is not named as the 2810.5 'other entity' and is not treated as a defendant on this packet.
note: Prospective Cluster 5 employment matter. Ripens only if a non-hire or rescission rests on registry information. First Advantage is in the packet for drug/alcohol testing; user also records FA as conducting the background search. Do not collapse the drug screen into a Megan's Law consumer report. Watch: the missing standalone ICRAA §1786.16 / FCRA consumer-report authorization; pre-adverse and adverse notice cadence if a report issues; whether any rescission cites NSOPW, Megan's Law, or SOURCE OF RECORD: CALIFORNIA SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY. Calendar Sep. 23 (anticipated start). If he starts, this is no longer a failure-to-hire file. Uber AV stays a campaign watch until a decision-file shows Uber set a registry screen or jointly made the hire/no-hire call. The MAA is live; a 290.46 / ICRAA / FCRA non-hire is the fight they will try to send to arbitration.
procedural_status: PENDING / pre-dispute. No complaint, no demand, no CRD charge. Offer of Temporary Employment accepted Sep. 14, 2026. Anticipated start Sep. 23, 2026. Next: preserve any pre-adverse/adverse notices and the missing consumer-report disclosure if it arrives; do not treat a drug-screen FA letter as the registry report.
risk: Monitoring file, not a claim. First Advantage is named for drug/alcohol testing; a consumer/registry report from FA would make the 25/26 notice format turnkey, but use is still unproven and no such report is in hand.
